one_line: Tamil Sangam-age poet who painted bustling Pandya Madurai in the long poem Maduraikanchi.

appearance.face: Oval face with warm brown complexion, sharp straight nose, neatly groomed short beard and mustache, slightly arched brows and large thoughtful anime-style eyes; default expression calm, observant and faintly smiling, as if always noticing city details.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair oiled and gathered into a small low knot at the back of the head, front kept smooth with a short central forelock; a narrow white cotton headband tied around the forehead with small knot at the back, ends short.
appearance.costume: He wears a finely woven, ankle-length off-white cotton veshti wrapped around the waist and pleated in front, border woven in a narrow dark-maroon stripe, paired with a light, full-sleeved upper cloth (thin cotton angavastram-style) in pale cream draped over both shoulders and chest, the right end occasionally tucked at the waist; on his neck a simple long tulasi-bead style wooden mala, on his wrists two thin plain copper bangles, and on his ankles a single slim copper anklet on the left leg; his feet are in simple dark-brown leather sandals with toe loop and strap; over one shoulder he carries a rolled palm-leaf bundle tied with a dark-brown cotton cord, and the fabric shows subtle cross-weave texture without printed patterns.
appearance.signature: A neatly bound stack of palm-leaf manuscripts in a light-brown wooden cover, tied with a single dark-maroon cord, often held in his left hand or tucked under his arm.

ref_desc: Mankudi Maruthanar is a mid-30s, lean, warm-brown-complexioned Tamil poet with an oval face, short beard, black hair in a low knot with a white headband, wearing an off-white veshti with dark-maroon border, pale-cream long-sleeved upper cloth, simple copper ornaments, brown sandals, and carrying a bound palm-leaf manuscript stack tied with a dark-maroon cord.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Mankudi Maruthanar, a Sangam-age Tamil poet in 2nd–3rd century CE Madurai: a lean man in his mid-30s with warm brown skin, oval face, sharp straight nose, short neatly kept beard and mustache, large thoughtful eyes and slightly arched brows, calm observant faintly smiling expression. His thick black hair is oiled and gathered into a small low knot at the back, front smooth with a short central forelock, and he wears a narrow white cotton headband tied around his forehead. He is dressed in an ankle-length off-white cotton veshti wrapped and pleated in front with a narrow dark-maroon woven border, and a light, full-sleeved pale-cream cotton upper cloth draped modestly over both shoulders and chest, one end sometimes tucked at his waist, the cloth showing subtle cross-weave texture only. Around his neck is a simple long wooden-bead mala, with two thin plain copper bangles on his wrists and a single slim copper anklet on his left ankle. His feet are in simple dark-brown leather sandals with a toe loop and strap. In his left hand, or tucked under his arm, he carries his signature prop: a neatly bound stack of palm-leaf manuscripts in a light-brown wooden cover tied with a single dark-maroon cord. Show him front-facing, full-body, with clear views of face, hair knot and headband, draped garments, ornaments, sandals and the manuscript bundle, using a palette of warm brown, off-white, dark maroon, pale cream and dark brown.
